newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares close lower in listless, shaky trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares close lower in listless, shaky trade.

text.p: Share prices finished lower at Bombay bourses on Tuesday pulled down by foreign funds which sold blue-chip stocks ahead of year end, brokers said.
"FIIs (foreign institutional investors) were sellers in pivotals," said Sunil Kothari at brokerage Nagindas Kothari. "Buyers were very choosy."
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) closed 17.21 points, or 0.61 percent, lower at a provisional 2,797.85.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index was down 1.72 points, or 0.21 percent, at provisional 807.28 after dipping to 797.66.
Anglo-Dutch multinational stock Hindustan Lever and scooter-maker Bajaj Auto were sold by the FIIs, traders said. Hindustan Lever dropped 12.75 rupees to 772.25 and Bajaj Auto shed 9.75 to 672.
Traders said the fear of more defaults after three brokers at the NSE were declared defaulters on Monday undermined sentiment and kept buyers away.
They said some brokers were facing difficulty to honour obligations after a slump in share prices saddled them with huge losses.
The NSE said the defaults will not hit clients because the exchange had a settlement guarantee system.
State-run BHEL bucked the trend rallying 9.25 rupees to 221 on news the electrical engineering firm was bidding for big captive power plants.
Ranbaxy fell 11 rupees to 524, Nestle 6.0 to 185, TISCO 1.75 to 150, SBI 3.25 to 204.25 and L&T 2.25 to 199.
